entrypoints.summary: The GET name parameter is accepted only when it is a string shorter than 128 bytes, then echoed unescaped into the HTML greeting and hashed with crc32b for the response CSP nonce.

relation_candidates.rationale: The reflected name value is both the content hashed by crc32b and the place where the attacker embeds the nonce candidate.
The solver accepts a payload only when its embedded nonce candidate equals the completed payload CRC32, matching the server-generated CSP nonce.
The author describes sending the working URL to the administrator and using window.open or location from the executing payload to exfiltrate cookies.
The writeup explicitly identifies exfiltration of the administrator's cookies as the post-execution action.
The writeup states that sending the working URL to the administrator results in obtaining the flag; bot implementation and the precise dependency are uninspected.
A nonce independent of attacker-controlled markup removes the equality condition used by the fixed-point search.
Escaping the name value prevents supplied script markup from becoming a script element in the response.

impact.affected_asset: Administrator browser session cookies and the CTF flag protected by the administrator workflow.
impact.attacker_capability: Construct a self-consistent reflected script payload, submit its URL to the administrator, and execute that payload on the administrator visit.
impact.security_effect: CSP-authorized execution of attacker-injected JavaScript in a visiting administrator's page context, with writeup-reported cookie exfiltration and flag retrieval.

causal_trace.summary: An attacker supplies a string-valued, sub-128-byte name parameter containing HTML markup; the page reflects the value without HTML escaping.
The server derives the script-src nonce deterministically as crc32b(name), where name is attacker-controlled reflected content, rather than using independent authorization material.

A search substitutes each eight-hex-digit candidate into an injected script nonce and accepts a payload when the CRC32 of the completed payload equals that embedded candidate; the resulting script nonce matches the nonce emitted in the CSP.

The author writeup states that the matching injected script executes; after the crafted URL is sent to the administrator, navigation-based exfiltration is used because default-src is none, and the challenge flag is obtained. Admin-bot and cookie configuration were not inspected.

primary_invariant.kind: CSP nonce authorization independence and unpredictability
primary_invariant.statement: A script authorization nonce must be independent of attacker-controlled reflected markup and unavailable for an attacker to synthesize into injected markup before the response is produced.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The application calculates the nonce as crc32b of the attacker-supplied name that is also emitted verbatim into the response, allowing construction or search of a self-consistent payload whose nonce equals its completed-payload CRC32.

raw_refs.role: challenge-author writeup, embedded PHP source, and solver

quality.review_notes: The embedded PHP excerpt and author-provided CRC32 fixed-point brute-forcer substantiate the input-to-CSP mechanism. The official artifact inspected here is only a directory page; raw application, deployment, and adminbot.js were not inspected. The writeup reports admin cookie exfiltration and flag retrieval, but no captured execution result or bot/cookie configuration is present. No remediation patch exists in the bundle; mitigation is an invariant-based recommendation.

remediation.invariant_restored: The script authorization token is generated independently of attacker-controlled markup, and attacker input is rendered as text rather than executable markup.
mitigation_classes: generate a cryptographically random per-response CSP nonce independent of request content

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The attacker prepares a script-bearing name payload with an eight-hex-character nonce slot, searches for a candidate equal to the CRC32 of the fully substituted payload, and supplies the resulting value through the name parameter.
data_structure_invariants: The name parameter must be a string shorter than 128 bytes to replace the default value.
The script nonce embedded in a successful payload equals the crc32b hash of the complete reflected name value.

numeric_domains.attacker_constraints: The documented brute force ranges from 0 through 0xFFFFFFFF and formats each candidate as eight lowercase hexadecimal characters.
numeric_domains.name: nonce candidate

state_context.state_machine: The response accepts a constrained name value, computes a CRC32-based nonce from that same value, and renders the value into HTML while authorizing scripts bearing the computed nonce.

target.component: PHP greeting page and its Content-Security-Policy nonce construction
